title: Fix a caption one word at a time, on the canvas and in a word lane
goal: Captions that write themselves get some words wrong, and today the only fix is retyping a whole caption. Let a person double-click one wrong word to fix just that word, and see every word as its own small block on the captions track that they can drag earlier or later and stretch, the way the captions mock draws it. The user asked for this after captioning a real recording.
notes:
Filed from the intake window.

The user's words, 2026-09-25: 'It misspelled some words, and I'd like to adjust them. I tried double clicking on an individual word that was wrong and couldn't edit. I could only edit captions as a whole. I also wanted to resize the individual words and drag them within the captions timeline but couldn't.'

Where things are (moved out of the goal by the 2026-09-25 triage): the model already has word timing (TranscribedWord startMS/endMS in Sources/PhotonzCore/Captions.swift, CaptionCue.words, the active-word highlight in CaptionLook.swift), but no UI edits a single word. The mock docs/design/mocks/pages/video-captions.html draws a word lane (.lane.wordlane, .wchip) with a chip per word on its own time span; its open question 'inline nudge on each word chip, or re-transcription plus a global offset?' is answered by the user: per word, inline. Build it at the mock's fidelity; runner-prompt rules on default config, side-by-side with the mock, labels-not-explanations and right-click apply. Ask: would someone fixing captions in Premiere or Descript get this, and is it quicker here?
acceptance: Double-clicking a word in a caption on the canvas, or its chip in the word lane, edits just that word in place; Return or clicking away commits, Escape cancels, and the word keeps its timing
Correcting a word into two ('alot' to 'a lot') or merging two splits or joins the time span evenly, and the edit is one undo step
The captions track expands (chevron) into a word lane with one chip per word, as the mock draws it; the active word lights up as the playhead moves

Dragging a word chip moves that word AND every later word in its caption along with it, keeping their spacing, so a caption whose timing is off from one word on is fixed in one drag (user: 'grab "the" and move it to the left or right and all of the words after it move along with it'). Shift-drag carries every later caption on the track too, Premiere-ripple style; Cmd-drag moves the single word alone, clamped between its neighbours. Dragging a chip's edge resizes only that word. Everything snaps to the playhead and neighbouring words, words never overlap, and the whole drag is one undo step
Right-click a word: Edit Word, Split Here, Merge with Next, Delete Word, Move to Next Line, Play From Here
Tab and Shift-Tab step to the next and previous word while editing, so a run of typos is fixed without the mouse
Editing a word never re-styles or reflows the rest of the caption, and the fixed spelling survives re-captioning of a different stretch
A walk at Next defaults opens a captioned recording, fixes a misspelled word by double-clicking it on the canvas, fixes another in the word lane, drags and resizes a word, and photographs each step

log.note: User 2026-09-25: dragging a word must carry the words after it (example: 'the video captions' off from 'the'; drag 'the' and the rest follow). Acceptance updated: plain drag ripples the rest of the caption, Shift-drag ripples later captions, Cmd-drag moves one word.

triage 2026-09-25: goal rewritten in plain words; the user's quote and the code pointers moved to notes, nothing dropped. Related: picking-or-retyping-a-caption-answers-at-once measured 120 to 200 ms to pick or open a caption; fixing words one after another will feel that lag, so keep each word pick and open under 50 ms and say in the audit what it measured.

Reproduced 2026-09-25 on the probe at Next defaults (openSampleTalk + captionsWaitForThemselves, /tmp/wordrepro/repro.json): double-clicking 'The' on the canvas twice opens the WHOLE caption for typing with every word selected (captionsExpectEditingOnCanvas: 'typing into The transport bar and the timeline appear'). The Words lane already draws one chip per word and lights the active one, but only takes a click (playhead); no edit, drag, resize or right-click. Recogniser wrote 'Fodons' for 'Photonz', a real misspelling to fix in the walk. Pre-build review: Premiere's caption editing and Descript both edit a word in place and let you drag word timing; nothing in the mock collides with existing gestures except the lane click (kept: single click still moves the playhead, drag now moves the word). Most chips at Fit zoom are ~20pt wide so their letters are hidden; editing works on any chip, and the field opens wider than the chip.

Built and walked. Design change found by the walk: spoken words sit end to end, so a word carried earlier squeezes the word before it (down to 40 ms) instead of stopping at it; otherwise the user's own example (grab 'the', move it left) could not move at all. Command-drag and edge drags stay clamped. Left rough, not filed (each is a mock-fidelity nit the audit puts to the user, and no open task covers it): flat accent on the lit chip vs the mock's gradient; no second gridlines in the Words lane; no numeric readout while a chip is dragged; chips narrower than ~20 pt at Fit show no letters. Canvas right-click word menu shares its rows with the lane menu (verified through captionsWordSplitAndMerge) but was not opened by a walk: rightClick steps do not survive a lock and the rows are the same code.

Shipped in 907bc80a. Double-click a caption word on the picture or its chip on the Words lane to type over just that word (Return/click away keep, Escape cancels, Tab/Shift-Tab step across lines, two words split the time evenly). Words lane: drag carries the rest of the line (squeezing the word before when earlier), Shift ripples later lines, Command moves one word, edges stretch; snaps; one undo step. Right-click word menu on lane and picture. Fold arrow on the Captions track; chips lettered with ellipsis at the mock's 26 pt. Fixes survive Write Again via heardAs. Full suite green except VideoExportBudgetTests, failing identically on clean main (logged on the flake task). Audit queue/audits/2026-09-25-fix-a-caption-word.json.
